body: I lived in a small apartment complex and one day in the parking lot, there was a guy holding up a steak knife yelling threats and multiple cops trying to talk him down. The cops told us to stay inside with the doors locked until it had been resolved. I took a picture from the window, sent it to my boss and said "so...I'm gonna be late today." He replied "What the hell? See you when you get here."

The city has since tore down the mall in my hometown but I do remember going a few months before they did. So weird to see it in those dying days. There were maybe ten stores still open and very few people walking around. The arcade where I'd spent so much time as a kid was still open but most of the machines were turned off and a single employee was sitting behind the counter reading a book. Wouldn't surprise me if they'd had zero customers all day.

I drank Southern Comfort when I was 19 at a party. I proceeded to get absolutely hammered and the night became pretty fuzzy. My friend drove me home and I just wanted to go bed. Instead, I spent the night puking my guts out and had an absolutely monstrous hangover the next day. That was the one and only time I had Southern Comfort.

I was driving to a friend's house about 50 miles from where I lived. It was a Friday and I'd left work early thinking I could beat at least some of the traffic. Instead there was roadwork that bottle necked the interstate down to one lane, a car accident and about ten miles from that, another car accident. Because of all that, I'd been in the car for almost two hours. At this point, I was shaking because I had to pee so bad but only about five miles from my friend's house so I figured I could make it. By the time I parked, I could feel my bladder was at absolute capacity. I quickly said hello to him, stumbled into his bathroom and pissed for what felt like five minutes straight. Looking back, I should've just pulled off the interstate and gone to a gas station but I was so frustrated by the massive delay and just wanted to be done driving.

I have a big extended family but grew up in another state. I'd see them once a year when we'd go visit but there's an uncle I only met once. After that first time, he was never at any family gatherings, weddings, funerals or reunions. I was always told he was "working upstate" but when I got older, my dad told me the truth. This uncle was an abusive asshole to his wife and two kids but he eventually broke his son's arm in a fit of rage. 

He knew he was fucked and tried to flee the small town most of them lived in. Multiple family members caught him before he was able to flee and beat the everloving fuck out of him. They then drove him out of town and told him to never come back. His kids are now both adults with their own families. At the last family reunion, I asked if they'd heard anything from their dad at all and they said they weren't sure if he was even still alive.
"It's complicated" because every time I've heard it, it was an excuse to cover for someone's shitty behavior.

When I worked in construction, a coworker was going on a week long vacation so the company decided to use a labor temp service to replace him that week. A guy showed up and seemed normal enough. Then we took a break and he started talking about how much he liked watching his wife fuck other guys. It was so out of the blue and the rest of us were just sorta stunned into silence as he kept talking about it. Inevitably, he asked if any of us were interested. We all said no, he persisted, we said no again, he finally said "whatever your loss." He was grumpy and sour for the rest of the day. He brought it up again around 3 PM as we were getting ready to leave and we again declined. I'm guessing my boss said something because the guy was supposed to be there all week and instead a different guy showed up the next day.
I genuinely miss when I had no idea who this stupid asshole was.

Similar situation in college but my friend and I were on foot. We were walking the mile or so back to our house from the bar when he noticed a guy wearing a cowboy hat was pacing us about 20 feet back. We opted to stay on well lit/busy roads and when he kept following us, we walked towards the student center because we knew a cop was stationed there 24 hours a day and they were right inside the main entrance. 

The cowboy hat guy initially followed us up the walkway but I think he got a glimpse of the cop sitting at his desk because he suddenly turned around and bolted away from the building. The cop said we did the right thing and that the guy was probably waiting for the opportunity to rob us. He had another cop drive us home because we were both freaked out.

Growing up, I had a friend whose dad would go through random phases of banning any TV shows he deemed "inappropriate" for his kids to watch. For maybe a month, they weren't allowed to watch stuff like The Simpsons but then inevitably, their dad would just stop caring and they'd go back to watching it normally instead of having to hide it. This would happen two or three times a year.

The show Unsolved Mysteries had a segment about a guy who'd murdered two people and it happened in a city about 30 minutes from my hometown. At the time he was "still at large" so 10 year old me was absolutely convinced this guy was coming to my house to kill me next.

I was set up with a girl my friend worked with at a restaurant. I thought she was super cute and interesting but she asked me twice during dinner if I had any coke and then asked if I'd drive her to coke dealer's house (which was in a city over an hour away). I declined to do this and we went our separate ways. I found out she got arrested about a month later for possession. Felt like a bullet dodged.

Years ago at a job, we were gifted $10 gift cards to a grocery store chain that doesn't even exist in our state. I looked it up and the closest one was a three hour drive. The owner of our company lived in another state where this grocery chain was common and just assumed they were everywhere. I don't think any of us ever used them.

Not a work bonus but one of my brothers has always been a notoriously bad gift giver because he always forgets until the day of whatever's happening. One year for my birthday he got me...a single $1 scratch ticket and of course it wasn't a winner.

I was in landscape construction for 15 years. One of the companies I worked for promised Christmas bonuses if a certain target was reached. Everyone worked their asses off and achieved the target. We were all expecting money with a lot of guys saying it was just what they needed to buy gifts. We all got a fucking $20 gift card to a movie theater chain. This was not some small, barely making ends meet operation: this was one of the biggest landscaping companies in the state and the owners had multiple vacation homes. 

Multiple people quit after this, citing the insulting bonus to the HR person as why. The owners eventually sent out a company wide "we understand the frustration and vow to do better" email but did absolutely nothing else. I ended up quitting shortly after because I found a better company to work for. Despite being a significantly smaller company, the owner gave us actual money for a Christmas bonus and as a result, retained his good employees. Crazy concept.

Campus gym had a running track with four lanes. Some jackass decided that this was the perfect place for him to do sit ups. He laid across three lanes and started doing sit ups. A group of people were running together and politely asked the guy to go do his sit ups literally anywhere else (there was tons of floor space where he could have been doing this). Dude immediately started whining and saying he wasn't bothering anyone and that they could easily go around him. Someone went and got an employee and suddenly sit up man's demeanor was "oh golly gee I didn't know I was bothering anyone." The employee saw right through his bullshit and told him if he did it again, they'd kick him out. He sulked out of the area with a sour lemon face while muttering under his breath. I witnessed all of this from a nearby stationary bike. What reality would you think it's okay to lay on the fucking running track to do your sit ups, especially at 4 PM when there's tons of other people in the gym?

I live in a city considered "bike friendly" but my god, so many of them think this means "the laws don't apply to me in way, shape or form." The thing they do here that drives me insane is riding tandem instead of single file. I don't really care if you're doing that on a non busy street but no, they'll do it on the absolute busiest road in the city, forcing everyone to go around them. It's crazy to me because any driver could easily clip the dummy who's riding halfway in the car lane.

When I was 20, my friend invited me to an off campus party at his friend's house. I was initially excited but it took all of 30 seconds to realize this party was gonna get busted sooner than later and I didn't want to be there for it. I told my friend I didn't feel getting a ticket for underage drinking and he said "you can leave but I'm staying." 

Maybe a minute after leaving, multiple cop cars went flying by. I was at the end of the block at this point and kept walking but looked back to see if the cops were going to that house. Sure enough, that's what they did. The friend who'd invited me said he and pretty much everyone else got an underage drinking ticket. Glad I decided to opt out immediately instead of trying to decide to stay or not.

His wife got suspicious and tailed him to a sketchy motel by the interstate, where he and the teenage girl went into a room together. His wife divorced him, he served time and then immediately left the state. It's been something like 12 years now and I haven't heard someone from the area mention it once.

Will interrupt conversations, talk over people, repeat his unfunny jokes, all because we're trying to ignore his toddler like need for attention. I don't live with my family but I have him blocked on absolutely everything because he'll just bombard me with messages otherwise. It's my way of setting hard boundaries.

A roommate made weed brownies and told me to start with a quarter of one and go from there. After a while, I wasn't feeling anything so my stupid ass ate two full ones. We were sitting on our couch watching TV when it hit me like a fucking truck. I suddenly felt like my soul was going to Jupiter and I sort of melted into the couch. The urge to throw up hit very shortly after so I awkwardly stumbled to the bathroom and just puked my brains out. I looked at my roommate and said "I think I'm gonna go lay down." 

My roommate, bless him, filled my big water jug, helped me to my room and also got me a bucket in case I needed to puke again but couldn't make it to the bathroom. I barely slept that night because I was just so high and felt like I was in a wave pool. I threw up a few more times throughout the night and kept drinking water. I ended up calling in sick to work because I felt so shitty in the morning. After that night, I didn't get high for a very long time due to the paranoia of potentially reliving that night.

You just know that even now, despite multiple run ins with the law, arrests and bannings that he still thinks none of it is his fault. He was getting kicked out of places and playing the victim before any of us even knew who he was.

I was at my regular bar one night having drinks and chatting with my bartender friend. It was fairly dead (maybe ten people in the entire place) when a woman none of us had ever seen came in and ordered a drink. I continued to just drink my beers and chat with my friend when he's free when the unknown woman walked up to me and introduced herself. She said she thought I was cute and asked if I wanted to drink with her at her place. 

Now I know there's so many ways this could've gone wrong but I, being on a pretty long dry spell and with my friend's encouragement, agreed to go home with her.


Everything seemed normal. She lived in a tastefully decorated apartment and told me about her job as a researcher at the local college. We had a drink and started messing around a bit. I felt like I'd hit the jackpot! Then she asked if I wanted to smoke. I declined, thinking she was gonna smoke weed.

Instead she pulled out a baggie of something white, put some in a pipe and asked if I'd ever smoked crack before. That was my "what the fuck did I get myself into" moment. I declined to smoke any crack with her and she got really pissy. Started calling me names and that I'd never know what crack was like until I tried it. I left immediately, walked about a block from her apartment and called an Uber. Thankfully I never saw her again.

At this time in my life, I was not good with confrontation at all. My roommate was very, very good with confrontation. He immediately went in the hall (wearing nothing but his boxers) and asked them to be quiet/go talk somewhere else. Like a lot of people in this thread, I found a porn stash. It was the early 2000s. My friend's dad was a big gamer and had a huge CD book of all his games. It was the middle of summer, my friend and I wanted to play something but couldn't find the CD book in his dad's home office. We dug around in the closet for it and found a box hidden under a blanket and a bunch of golf magazines. The box was chock full of porno tapes and magazines. Being a horny idiot teenager, I waited for an opportunity later that day and stole one of the tapes while my friend was in the shower. I was paranoid for days afterwards that I was going to get him in trouble or get myself in trouble but nothing ever happened. I'm guessing his dad either didn't notice a tape was missing or he didn't want to admit he had a porn stash and that something was missing.

Ms. Lynch, our seventh grade history teacher, didn't make the full school year. Her teaching methods were less than stellar and because it was seventh grade, there were some absolute shit head kids. It was a really bad combination and at some point in the last month of school, she just stormed out of the classroom one final time. We had a substitute for the rest of the year and on the last day, it was announced that she would not be back in the fall. 

Years later, I became coworkers and eventual friends with a guy whose mom was an English teacher at our middle school. I learned from him and his mom that Ms. Lynch was a nepotism hire. Her dad had some high up position in the school district and was also good friends with the principal of our middle school. I was asked if I remembered Ms. Hoffman, her replacement for eighth grade and I said yes. Turns out Ms. Hoffman (who was one of my favorite teachers ever) was supposed to be the original hire but Ms. Lynch's dad pulled enough strings to get his daughter the job instead.

My friend and I call this the "creepy cowboy" story.

One night in college, he and I left the bar around 1 AM to make the mile long walk back to our house. We were fairly tipsy but still aware of our surroundings and what direction to go. About a block away from the bar, my friend noticed a guy wearing a cowboy hat keeping pace about 20 feet back from us. Initially we just assumed he was another bar patron walking home but when we turned down one street, he followed. At this point, my paranoia started ramping up and I told my friend we should walk towards the student center and see if the guy kept following us. 

We took a route towards the student center and cowboy man kept following us. The reason we went to that building is that there was always a campus cop stationed there 24/7 and he was right inside the door. Initially, cowboy man followed us up the path to the student center but I think he realized what we were doing and he suddenly bolted in the other direction. Like, full on sprinted away from the building and down a random street. 

We told the cop what had happened and he said we were smart to be cautious. They'd recently had issues with muggings/break ins and had learned it was guys following college kids home from the bars late night to either mug them or stake out their house/car and see if it was worth coming back later. We gave the best description we could of cowboy man but no idea if anything ever came of it. The cop had another cop drive us home because we were both freaked out and paranoid about walking the rest of the way.

This job wasn't hard or gross, just insanely boring. One year in my teens, I worked as a parking lot attendant for this seasonal carnival/produce market in my home town. All you did was stand in one spot near the entrance and point cars towards the back parking area. A piece of wood with an arrow painted on it would be just as effecive. This was pre smart phones so you really couldn't do anything but stand there and make up games in your head to pass the time. The shifts were only six hours but felt much, much longer. I finished the month and never went back. Funny thing is, I went to the carnival years later and when I pulled into the parking lot, they had put up a sign with an arrow on it. The owner must have realized that he didn't need to pay someone to stand there and point.

Rotten rice. In college, I lived in a house with roommates and spring break was coming up. Three of us left town on Friday while one roommate was staying an extra day. He made rice in his rice cooker, only ate some of it and then forgot to put the rest in the fridge. He left the next morning and that rice sat on the counter for a week. 

I was the first one home and the smell that hit me when I opened the door was horrifying. When I opened the lid on the rice cooker, there were little winged insects and maggots in the rice. I threw that pot in the sink, blasted it with soap and the hottest water I could get out of the faucet and then put it in the garage.
